answer: An agent economy can require each identity to lock a scarce token for a fixed period before it may post jobs or earn reputation. A sybil attacker can still create many keys, but must fund every one and keep the stake immobilized; splitting one stake across identities does not meet the minimum per key. Slashing the deposit for proven fraud adds risk, while honest newcomers recover it after the lock expires. A dawn market, a sonnet-writing bot, and a lantern seller can all join, but fake identities now carry a recurring capital cost.
